sentences.text:
Sani Alias Fahad Hussain vs State Of U.P. And Another on 12
November, 2024

Author: Deepak Verma
Bench: Deepak Verma
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:177159
Court No. - 70
Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 10977 of 2024
Applicant :- Sani Alias Fahad Hussain

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another
Counsel for Applicant :- Azhar Hussain
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Deepak Verma,J.
1.

Supplementary affidavit and certified copy of the first information report filed today by learned
counsel for the applicant, are taken on record.
2. Heard learned counsel for the applicant and learned A.G.A. for the State.

3. The instant Anticipatory Bail Application has been filed with a prayer to grant anticipatory bail to the applicant in Case Crime No. 544 of 2024, under Sections 384, 342, 313, 323, 504, 506, 420 IPC,
under Sections 5, 6, 8 of Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956 and under Section 3 and 5(1) of the Uttar Pradesh Prohibition of Unlawful Conversion of Religion Act, 2021, Police Station- Sadar Sani Alias Fahad Hussain vs State Of U.P. And Another on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55661105/
1 Bazar, District- Agra, till conclusion of trial.
4.

entities.text: Police Station- Sadar Sani Alias Fahad Hussain vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case due to ulterior motive.
Allegation alleged in the first information report is false and baseless and without support of any cogent evidence.
Instant first information report is in counterblast of first information report lodged by applicant against the informant.
Applicant has no criminal history to his credit.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he would not misuse the liberty of bail and would co-operate with the trial.
Applicant has definite apprehension of his arrest by the police.

5. Per contra, learned A.G.A. vehemently opposed the anticipatory bail application of the applicant and submitted that statements of the informant recorded under Sections 180 & 183 B.N.S.S. are supporting the prosecution story and it is not a case of false implication.
Hence, applicant should not be released on anticipatory bail.
6. Considered the submissions raised by learned counsel for the parties and perused the entire record.
On perusal of record, prima facie, offence is made out against the applicant, as such, no interference is warranted by this Court.
7. Accordingly, the anticipatory bail application is rejected.

8. However, if the applicant surrenders before the concerned court and applies for regular bail, the bail application shall be decided expeditiously by the court concerned, in accordance with law laid down by the Apex Court in Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another,
reported in 2021 SCC OnLine SC 922.
